heroHeadline: PLA De-Escalates to 2 Sorties on Apr 30 After 28-Sortie Peak — 5 PLAN Vessels Remain; Ex-US Intel Chief Urges Taiwan Legislature to Pass Defense Budget 'With Haste'; 14 Days to Trump-Xi Summit
heroSubtitle: Taiwan's MND detected just 2 PLA aircraft sorties and 5 PLAN vessels plus 2 official ships on April 30, 2026 — the lowest combined activity since the post-peak pullback and a sustained de-escalation from the 28-sortie non-exercise peak of April 26 (the highest non-exercise count since Justice Mission-2025). Both sorties entered Taiwan's southwestern ADIZ. The continued drawdown follows PLA's established oscillating pattern: 28 sorties (Apr 26) → 7 (Apr 27) → 10 (Apr 29) → 2 (Apr 30). With 14 days remaining before the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15), former US intelligence chiefs escalated pressure on Taiwan's legislature on April 30 to pass the NT$1.25 trillion special defense budget 'with all due haste,' the latest in a sustained US intervention campaign — following AIT Director Greene (Apr 27), INDOPACOM Admiral Paparo (Apr 22-23), and INDOPACOM Deputy Commander Thomas (Mar 27). Taiwan's defense budget deadlock continues: KMT at NT$800B cap vs. DPP's full NT$1.25T request, with Beijing expected to press Trump to limit arms sales at the summit. TSMC completed a $231M divestment of its Arm Holdings stake (April 29) as it reported a 58% Q1 profit surge and forecasts >30% full-year revenue growth — reinforcing Taiwan's 'silicon shield' strategic deterrence value. KMT legislators clashed internally on April 28 over the NT$800B budget cap, with some members signaling possible flexibility ahead of the summit.
